Catatonia was previously described as an abrupt and remarkable withdrawal from the senses and the environment in the context of a psychotic or mood disorder.

In general, catatonia is characterized by a change in movement and behavior, either increased, decreased, or abnormal, compared to baseline, in the context of intact physical capacity for motor movement.
Cases of catatonia associated with autoimmune encephalitis highlight the role of immune-mediated neural dysfunction.
Autoimmune processes, particularly anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis, have been implicated in the pathogenesis of catatonia.
